How to Use This Calculator

  1. Enter your outstanding balance, current rate and the term left, all from your latest statement
  2. Enter the new bank's rate and term. Keep the same term for a fair comparison of the rate
  3. Add the exit fee and the costs of the new loan, including processing, valuation and registration
  4. Check the net saving and the break-even point, then ask how long you expect to keep the loan

How the Comparison Works

Net saving = interest left on current loan − interest on new loan − all fees

The break-even point is the first month you would be ahead if you repaid the loan at that moment, counting payments made, debt left and fees. This is stricter than dividing the fees by the monthly saving, which can make a longer term look better than it is.

Example: AED 1,200,000 with 20 years left, moving from 5.75% to 4.75%, with AED 30,000 in total fees. The monthly payment falls from AED 8,425 to AED 7,755. You save AED 130,876 over the term after fees, and you break even in month 31.

These totals assume both rates hold for the full term. Most UAE mortgages move to a variable rate after a few years, so treat the result as a guide and try a rate closer to the likely long-run cost.

Costs to Ask About

  • Early settlement fee: charged by your current bank, and capped as described below
  • Bank processing fee: commonly quoted at up to about 1% of the loan, though promotions vary
  • Valuation: often around AED 2,500 to 3,500
  • Mortgage registration: widely quoted at 0.25% of the loan plus AED 290 in Dubai
  • Life and property insurance: a new policy may cost more or less, which changes your true saving

The Central Bank of the UAE capped early settlement fees at 1% of the outstanding balance or AED 10,000, whichever is lower, in a 2019 circular. Fee figures above are market estimates from 2026 and differ by bank and emirate.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a mortgage buyout in the UAE?
A buyout is when a new bank pays off your existing mortgage and takes over the loan, usually on a lower rate. You then repay the new bank. It is also called a loan takeover, a balance transfer or refinancing.
How much does a mortgage buyout cost?
Expect the early settlement fee on the old loan, plus the new loan's processing, valuation and mortgage registration costs. Mortgage registration at the Dubai Land Department is widely quoted at 0.25% of the loan plus AED 290. Some banks waive or absorb part of these costs, so ask for a written list.
What is the early settlement fee on a UAE mortgage?
A 2019 Central Bank of the UAE circular capped it at 1% of the outstanding balance or AED 10,000, whichever is lower. Some lenders may set different terms during a fixed period, so ask your bank for a settlement figure in writing.
When is a mortgage buyout worth it?
When the interest saved clearly exceeds the fees and you expect to keep the loan past the break-even point shown above. A lower rate on a small balance or a short remaining term may not recover the costs.
Should I compare the rate or the margin?
Both. An attractive fixed rate may only last a few years, after which the loan reverts to EIBOR plus a margin. To test that part of an offer, use the fixed to floating calculator linked below.
